title: Cain to the Flood, part 4 of 5: the waters recede
style: Classical oil painting on canvas, visible expressive brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, rich earthy palette of ochre, umber, olive and deep blue. The age of Noah and the great flood: people dressed in simple garments of rough undyed wool or animal skin, tools of wood, stone and bronze, nothing man-made beyond what the scene describes. Cinematic 16:9 landscape composition. No text, no borders, no watermark, no modern objects.

NOAH.name: Noah
NOAH.desc: Noah, a strong weathered man who looks about fifty, with warm brown skin, thick grey-streaked dark hair to his collar, a full grey-streaked beard, deep-set kind eyes and a lined brow, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough undyed brown wool with a leather belt and a darker wool mantle over one shoulder, and simple leather sandals

NOAH_WIFE.name: Noah's wife
NOAH_WIFE.desc: Noah's wife, a strong, kind-faced woman who looks about forty-five, with warm brown skin, grey-streaked black hair in one long thick braid over her shoulder, dark warm eyes and laughter lines, wearing an ankle-length dress of rough undyed cream wool with a brown wool shawl around her shoulders, and simple leather sandals

SHEM.name: Shem
SHEM.desc: Shem, a son of Noah, a lean, thoughtful man of about thirty with warm brown skin, wavy black hair to his jaw and a short neat black beard, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough undyed cream wool with a rope belt, and simple leather sandals

HAM.name: Ham
HAM.desc: Ham, a son of Noah, a stocky, broad-shouldered man of about thirty with warm brown skin, close-cropped curly black hair and a thick short black beard, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough rust-brown wool with a leather belt, and simple leather sandals

JAPHETH.name: Japheth
JAPHETH.desc: Japheth, a son of Noah, a tall, rangy man of about thirty with warm brown skin, long straight black hair tied back at the nape of his neck and a thin beard along his jaw, wearing a knee-length tunic of rough dark-grey wool with a leather belt, and simple leather sandals

blocks.GLORY: a vast radiance of pure golden-white light pouring down from above the frame, with no figure, no face and no human shape in the light
blocks.ONE: Exactly one person in the picture, no one else
blocks.TWO: Exactly two people in the picture, one man and one woman, no one else
blocks.NOLIGHTFIG: No figure, no face and no human shape in the light
blocks.ARK: the ark: an enormous, very long rectangular vessel like a great chest, built of dark timber coated black with pitch, with straight vertical sides, squared ends and a flat bottom resting on the ground, ten times as long as it is high, with a low-pitched plank roof, a narrow open gap running the whole length just under the eaves, and one large door in the middle of its long side; no mast, no sail, no oars, no rudder, no pointed prow, no curved hull and no windows in its sides
blocks.WIFE_S: Shem's wife, a slim woman in her twenties with warm brown skin and long black hair in two braids, wearing an ankle-length dress of rough undyed cream wool
blocks.WIFE_H: Ham's wife, a sturdy woman in her twenties with warm brown skin and curly black hair bound up in a rust-brown wool headcloth, wearing an ankle-length dress of rough rust-brown wool
blocks.WIFE_J: Japheth's wife, a tall woman in her twenties with warm brown skin and straight black hair in one long plait down her back, wearing an ankle-length dress of rough dark-grey wool
blocks.ARKFLOAT: the ark afloat: an enormous, very long rectangular vessel like a great chest, built of dark timber coated black with pitch, with straight vertical sides and squared ends, riding low and level in the water, ten times as long as it is high, with a low-pitched plank roof, a narrow open gap running the whole length just under the eaves, and one large door, shut tight, in the middle of its long side; no mast, no sail, no oars, no rudder, no pointed prow, no curved hull, no windows in its sides and no one on its roof
blocks.INSIDE: inside the ark: a long low deck of heavy dark timber with stout posts and beams and rows of wooden stalls and pens strewn with straw, lit by small clay oil lamps, with no windows
blocks.NOLAND: No land, no shore, no trees and no rocks anywhere, only water to every horizon
blocks.NODEAD: No bodies, no people and no animals anywhere in the picture
blocks.CALM: The animals are calm and unafraid, and none is led, roped or driven
blocks.ARKREST: the ark aground: an enormous, very long rectangular vessel like a great chest, built of dark timber coated black with pitch, with straight vertical sides, squared ends and a flat bottom resting level on a broad shoulder of bare rock high among mountains, ten times as long as it is high, with a low-pitched plank roof, a narrow open gap running the whole length just under the eaves, and one large door in the middle of its long side; no mast, no sail, no oars, no rudder, no pointed prow, no curved hull and no windows in its sides
blocks.HATCH: a small square hatch in the low-pitched plank roof of the ark, its wooden shutter swung open
blocks.ROOF: the long, low-pitched, black pitch-coated plank roof of the ark
blocks.NOBOW: No rainbow anywhere in the sky
blocks.ONEBIRD: Exactly one bird in the picture
blocks.PEAKS: bare wet rocky mountaintops standing out of the water like islands
blocks.ALTAR: a low square altar built of rough unhewn field stones piled without mortar, about waist high, with no carving and no steps
blocks.EIGHT: Exactly eight people: four men and four women, no children, no one else
blocks.SONS8: their three grown sons, three bearded men of about thirty in wool tunics of cream, rust-brown and dark grey, and the sons' three young wives in long wool dresses
blocks.DOORWAY: the one large open timber doorway in the towering black pitch-coated wall of the ark, whose sill lies level with a slope of bare dry rock
blocks.EMPTY: A pure landscape with no human being in it: not one person, figure or silhouette anywhere, near or far
blocks.FLATWALL: the flat, straight, vertical black pitch-coated plank wall of the ark, flat like the side of a great chest and not curved like a ship

segs.text: But God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark. And God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to subside.
The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
The waters receded steadily from the earth, and after 150 days the waters had gone down.
On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
And the waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible.
After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.
Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the waters had receded from the surface of the ground.

But the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned to him in the ark, because the waters were still covering the surface of all the earth. So he reached out his hand and brought her back inside the ark.
Noah waited seven more days and again sent out the dove from the ark.
And behold, the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak. So Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
And Noah waited seven more days and sent out the dove again, but this time she did not return to him.

In Noah’s six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters had dried up from the earth. So Noah removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was fully dry.
Then God said to Noah,
Come out of the ark, you and your wife, along with your sons and their wives.
Bring out all the living creatures that are with you—birds, livestock, and everything that crawls upon the ground—so that they can spread out over the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon it.
So Noah came out, along with his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives.
Every living creature, every creeping thing, and every bird—everything that moves upon the earth—came out of the ark, kind by kind.
Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. And taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.
When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, He said in His heart,
Never again will I curse the ground because of man, even though every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth. And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done.
As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.

stills.prompt: But God remembered Noah: a vast calm silver-grey sea under a heavy sky, and alone on it, small in the distance, {ARKFLOAT}; the clouds above it part and {GLORY}, falls on the ark alone. {NOLAND}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOBOW}. Very wide view.

God remembered Noah: {INSIDE}, where {NOAH}, sits on a timber bench and lifts his face as one thin shaft of golden daylight falls from above through a crack between the roof planks onto his face. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium close view.

And all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark: {INSIDE}, with animals in the stalls on both sides lifting their heads all together, two oxen, two sheep, two donkeys and two deer, and pairs of doves on the beams above. {NOPEOPLE}. Wide interior view down the length of the deck.

And God sent a wind over the earth: a great wind tearing across an endless grey sea, flattening the wave tops into long white streaks of spray and driving ragged clouds fast across the sky, and far off {ARKFLOAT}. {NOLAND}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Very wide low view over the water.

And the waters began to subside: an underwater view in clear green light, looking across the submerged bare rocky summit of a mountain; long bright rays of sunlight slant down through the water onto the rock, and the rippling surface is close above it. {NODEAD}. No fish. No boats. Wide underwater view.

The springs of the deep were closed: an underwater view in dim blue-green light of a long fissure in the rocky floor of the deep; the last thin threads of bubbles rise from the crack and fade away, and fine silt settles over still, quiet stone. {NODEAD}. No fish. Wide underwater view.

The floodgates of the heavens were closed: seen from the surface of a grey sea looking up, the last ragged openings in a black ceiling of cloud drawing shut, the final thin veils of falling water fading to mist, and pale daylight spreading behind the thinning cloud. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOLAND}. {NOBOW}. Low-angle very wide view.

And the rain from the sky was restrained: a close view along the black pitch-coated eaves of the ark's plank roof, the last few drops of rainwater hanging and falling from the edge of the planks, and beyond them a smooth grey sea under a brightening sky with no rain falling. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Close view.

The waters receded steadily from the earth: a blue-grey sea under broken clouds and long shafts of sunlight, the wind still ruffling the water, and {ARKFLOAT}, seen whole from the side, drifting. {NOLAND}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Very wide view.

After 150 days the waters had gone down: {INSIDE}, where {NOAH}, stands before a timber post covered from top to bottom with long rows of small plain knife notches, running his fingertips slowly down the rows. {ONE}. Medium close view.

The ark came to rest: an underwater view in clear green light. The underside of the ark is one vast, perfectly flat rectangle of dark timber planks, flat as a raft, with square corners, no keel and no curve; it is settling straight down onto a broad submerged shelf of bare rock, and a cloud of pale silt puffs out along its whole length where the flat wood meets the stone. It is a box, not a boat. {NODEAD}. No fish. Wide underwater view from the side.

The ark came to rest: {INSIDE}. In the middle of the deck {NOAH}, and {NOAH_WIFE}, have stumbled and both hold on to the same stout timber post, looking at each other in surprise, while a clay oil lamp hanging from a beam above them swings hard to one side. Solid timber walls close them in on every side: no openings, no daylight and nothing of the outside to be seen. {TWO}. Medium view.

On the mountains of Ararat: seen from high above, {ARKFLOAT}, lying perfectly still on calm clear water, and through the water all around and beneath it the dark shape of a great drowned mountain ridge can be seen, still wholly under the surface. No land above the water anywhere. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. High wide view looking down.

And the waters continued to recede: a close low view along {FLATWALL}, standing motionless in calm water, with a broad pale band of dried salt and silt on the timbers above the waterline showing how far the water has fallen. Beyond the wall there is only open water to the horizon: no land, no hills, no rocks and no shore. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Low medium view at the waterline.

The tops of the mountains became visible: the first dark rocky mountaintops breaking through the surface of a wide calm sea in early light, water streaming white down their bare wet sides, more points of rock just appearing far beyond them. No trees and no grass. No boats and no ark. {NODEAD}. {NOBOW}. Very wide view.

{EMPTY}. On the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible: a huge black timber box, the ark, standing aground on a high shoulder of wet bare rock with the sea lying close below it. The ark is a plain, very long rectangular chest with flat vertical walls, square corners, a flat bottom and a low-pitched plank roof, ten times as long as it is high, its one door shut; it is a box, not a boat: no curved hull, no pointed prow, no raised ends. All around to the horizon stand {PEAKS}. No trees and no grass. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Very wide view.

After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark: in the dim lamplit loft just under the plank roof of the ark, {NOAH}, standing on a short timber ladder, pushes up with one hand against a small square wooden shutter set in the roof planks above his head, thin bright lines of daylight showing around its edges. {ONE}. Low-angle medium view.

Noah opened the window: seen from outside on {ROOF}, {NOAH}, shown only from the chest up as he rises through {HATCH}, narrowing his eyes against the daylight, the wind lifting his hair; far behind him lie calm water and {PEAKS}. {ONE}. {NOBOW}. Medium view.

And sent out a raven: seen from outside on {ROOF}, {NOAH}, shown from the chest up in {HATCH}, lifts both hands high and lets go of {RAVEN}, which beats upward from his open hands with wings spread wide. {ONE}. {ONEBIRD}. {NOBOW}. Low-angle medium view.

{EMPTY}. It kept flying back and forth: {RAVEN}, flying low and strongly over a wide sheet of grey water between {PEAKS}, its dark reflection racing beneath it. {ONEBIRD}. No boats. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Wide view from the air.

Back and forth, until the waters had dried up from the earth: at dusk, {RAVEN}, wheeling in the air high above {ARKREST}, its door shut, the sea lying below its rock under a dull red sky. {ONEBIRD}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Wide low-angle view.

Then Noah sent out a dove: a close view of {NOAH}, holding {DOVE}, gently in both weathered hands against his chest and looking down at her, in soft daylight falling from above. {ONE}. {ONEBIRD}. Close view.

To see if the waters had receded from the surface of the ground: seen from outside on {ROOF}, {NOAH}, shown from the chest up in {HATCH}, lets {DOVE}, fly from his open palms, her white wings spread wide against grey water and sky. {ONE}. {ONEBIRD}. {NOBOW}. Medium view.

But the dove found no place to rest her foot: {DOVE}, flying low over grey water that fills the whole picture, searching. Nothing but water beneath her and around her: no branch, no rock, no shore. {ONEBIRD}. No boats. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium-wide view from the air, looking down at the water.

No place to rest her foot: a close view of {DOVE}, hovering wearily just above rippling grey water, her small pink feet reaching down toward the surface and finding only water. {ONEBIRD}. No branch, no rock. {NOPEOPLE}. Close view.

And she returned to him in the ark: seen from just behind {DOVE}, who flies in the foreground low over {ROOF}, which fills the lower half of the picture and runs away into the distance; far ahead on the roof {NOAH}, small in the distance and shown from the chest up in {HATCH}, waits with one arm raised. Only the roof of the ark is seen, not its sides, and grey water lies beyond it. {ONE}. {ONEBIRD}. {NOBOW}. Wide view from behind the bird.

{EMPTY}. Because the waters were still covering the surface of all the earth: grey water lying wide and flat over the drowned lands under a low sky, its surface broken only by a few far points of bare rock; no trees, no grass and no dry valley anywhere. No boats and no ark. {NODEAD}. {NOBOW}. Very wide view from low over the water.

So he reached out his hand and brought her back inside the ark: a close view from outside on {ROOF}, {NOAH}, shown from the chest up in {HATCH}, stretching one arm far out with his palm open, and {DOVE}, alighting on his open hand with her wings still half spread. {ONE}. {ONEBIRD}. Close view.

Noah waited seven more days: {INSIDE}, where {NOAH}, sits on a timber bench beneath a shaft of daylight falling from above, with {DOVE}, perched quietly on his raised wrist, the two looking at each other. {ONE}. {ONEBIRD}. Medium view.

And again sent out the dove from the ark: seen from inside the ark looking straight up through {HATCH}, to a square of bright morning sky; the raised arms of {NOAH}, seen from below and behind, reach up into the square of light as {DOVE}, flies up and away out of his hands. {ONE}. {ONEBIRD}. Low-angle view looking up.

And behold, the dove returned to him in the evening: {DOVE}, flying toward us across a red-gold evening sky over darkening water, with one small green leaf in her beak, and the low sun behind her. {ONEBIRD}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Medium-wide view.

With a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak: a close portrait of {DOVE}, in warm evening light, holding in her beak one single fresh green olive leaf, narrow and silvery underneath. Only one leaf: not a twig, not a branch, no olives. {ONEBIRD}. {NOPEOPLE}. Very close view of the bird's head and breast.

A freshly plucked olive leaf: a close view of {NOAH}, in warm evening light, holding up one single small green olive leaf between his finger and thumb and gazing at it in wonder. Only one leaf: not a twig, not a branch. {ONE}. No birds. Close view, face and hand.

So Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth: {INSIDE}, where {NOAH}, holds out one small green olive leaf on his open palm to {NOAH_WIFE}, who bends close over it with one hand lifted to her mouth, smiling. {TWO}. Medium close view.

The waters had receded from the earth: an old olive tree on a muddy hillside newly risen from the flood, its grey trunk streaked with dried silt, fresh green leaves opening on its branches in evening light, and the water lying far below in the valley. {NOPEOPLE}. No boats. {NOBOW}. Medium-wide view.

And Noah waited seven more days and sent out the dove again: at dawn, seen from outside on {ROOF}, {NOAH}, shown from the chest up in {HATCH}, lifts {DOVE}, high on his open hands toward a clear pale-gold sky. {ONE}. {ONEBIRD}. {NOBOW}. Low-angle medium view.

Sent out the dove again: {DOVE}, small and bright, flying away from us over mountain slopes and valleys where the water has drawn back and the first thin green shows on the earth, toward a far sunlit horizon. {ONEBIRD}. {NOPEOPLE}. No boats and no ark. {NOBOW}. Very wide view from the air.

But this time she did not return to him: at evening, seen from outside on {ROOF}, {NOAH}, shown from the chest up in {HATCH}, looks up into a wide empty evening sky with one open hand still half raised and empty, a quiet smile on his face. {ONE}. No birds anywhere. {NOBOW}. Medium view.

In Noah's six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month: sunrise over range upon range of bare mountains with white mist lying in the valleys, and on a high rocky shoulder in the middle distance {ARKREST}, its door shut. No water around the ark. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Very wide view.

The waters had dried up from the earth: a broad valley floor from which the flood has drained, a river running again in its own winding bed between wide flats of drying mud, with a few last shallow pools shining in the sun. No trees yet, only bare earth. {NODEAD}. No boats. {NOBOW}. Wide high view.

So Noah removed the covering from the ark: on top of {ROOF}, {NOAH}, standing in a long gap he has opened in the roof, heaves a broad black roof plank up and aside with both arms, other loosened planks stacked beside him, and bright sky behind. {ONE}. {NOBOW}. Low-angle medium-wide view.

Noah removed the covering from the ark: {INSIDE}, but now a long strip of the roof above has been taken away and bright sunlight pours down through the opening onto the deck, where {NOAH}, and {NOAH_WIFE}, stand side by side with their faces lifted into the light, she shading her eyes with her hand. {TWO}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium-wide view.

And saw that the surface of the ground was dry: seen from behind and a little above, {NOAH}, standing waist-deep in a long gap in {ROOF}, both hands on the edge of the planks, looking out and down over a mountainside of bare, pale, dry earth and rock that falls away to dry valleys far below. No water in sight. {ONE}. {NOBOW}. Wide view over his shoulder.

The earth was fully dry: a close view of ground that was flood mud, now dried pale and hard and split into a web of cracks, with small bright green shoots pushing up through the cracks in warm sunlight. {NOPEOPLE}. Close view of the ground.

By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was fully dry: a wide mountain valley in clear sunlight, its slopes dry and touched with new green grass, streams running in their beds, and high above on a rocky shoulder {ARKREST}, its door shut. No flood water anywhere. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Very wide view.

Then God said to Noah: {INSIDE}, where a long strip of the roof above has been taken away, and through the opening {GLORY}, falls on {NOAH}, who stands alone on the deck with his face lifted and his hands open at his sides. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium-wide low-angle view.

Come out of the ark: seen from inside the dark ark, {NOAH}, seen from behind, pushing the one great timber door outward with both hands, a tall blaze of daylight opening in front of him and spilling across the deck planks. {ONE}. Medium-wide view from inside.

You and your wife, along with your sons and their wives: seen from outside, four married couples standing close together in sunlight on bare dry rock in front of {DOORWAY}, each husband with his wife beside him, all looking out and up into the light: {NOAH}, with {NOAH_WIFE}; {SHEM}, with {WIFE_S}; {HAM}, with {WIFE_H}; and {JAPHETH}, with {WIFE_J}. {EIGHT}. No tools. {NOBOW}. Wide view.

Bring out all the living creatures that are with you: {INSIDE}, where {NOAH}, swings open the wooden gate of a straw-filled stall and two brown oxen step out past him toward daylight at the far end of the deck. Exactly one person and two oxen. Medium view.

Birds: flocks of birds pouring up into a bright sky out of a long gap opened in {ROOF}: white doves, black ravens, storks and small brown sparrows, each kind flying with its own kind. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Low-angle wide view.

Livestock, and everything that crawls upon the ground: seen close and low on sunlit bare rock, two tortoises and two green lizards crawling away from us in the foreground, and just beyond them the legs and hooves of sheep and goats walking past in the same direction. {NOPEOPLE}. Close low view.

So that they can spread out over the earth: seen from high on the mountain, herds and flocks of many kinds of animals fanning out and down a wide dry mountainside into a broad green valley, deer bounding ahead, cattle and sheep following, birds flying above them. {CALM}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Very wide high view.

And be fruitful and multiply upon it: in fresh spring grass, a ewe standing over two small newborn lambs, one of them struggling up onto its legs, in warm sunlight. Exactly three sheep: one ewe and two lambs. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium close view.
So Noah came out: {NOAH}, stepping out of {DOORWAY}, onto the rock, his leading foot just touching the ground and the sunlight full on his lifted face. {ONE}. {NOBOW}. Medium-wide low-angle view.

Along with his sons and his sons' wives: three couples walking out of the open doorway of the ark onto a slope of bare dry rock in bright sunlight, looking around them in wonder: {SHEM}, with {WIFE_S}; {HAM}, with {WIFE_H}; and {JAPHETH}, with {WIFE_J}. Exactly six people: three men and three women, no children, no one else. {NOBOW}. Medium-wide view.

And his wife: on an open mountainside of dry earth and new grass in bright sunlight, {NOAH_WIFE}, kneels and presses both open hands flat on the dry ground, smiling, while {NOAH}, stands beside her with his hand on her shoulder. Behind them are only mountains and sky: no ark, no ship and no building in the picture. {TWO}. {NOBOW}. Medium view.

Every living creature came out of the ark, kind by kind: animals walking out through one large open timber doorway in {FLATWALL}, onto a slope of bare dry rock, in groups, each kind keeping with its own kind: first a maned lion and a lioness, behind them two oxen, behind them two deer. Exactly six animals. {CALM}. {NOPEOPLE}. Medium-wide view straight at the wall.

Every creeping thing: a close low view of sunlit dry earth and new grass over which two snails, two beetles and two small brown lizards creep away from the dark shadow of the ark's wall into the light. {NOPEOPLE}. Close low view.

And every bird: flocks rising into a clear sky above the mountains, each kind in its own flock: a flock of white storks, a flock of black ravens, a flock of grey doves and a pair of eagles soaring higher than all. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Low-angle very wide view.

Everything that moves upon the earth came out of the ark, kind by kind: seen from far across the mountainside, {ARKREST}, its door standing open, and from the door a long line of animals winding away down the slope in separate groups, each kind by itself, with flocks of birds above. {CALM}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOBOW}. Very wide view.

Then Noah built an altar to the LORD: on open ground on the mountainside, {NOAH}, bending to set one more large rough stone on top of {ALTAR}, which he is building, more loose stones lying at his feet. {ONE}. No fire yet. {NOBOW}. Medium-wide view.

And taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird: {NOAH}, standing beside {ALTAR}, on which dry firewood is laid, with one hand resting on the neck of a horned ram; a young bull and a goat stand quietly near him, and two grey doves perch on his other forearm. No knife and no fire. {ONE}. {NOBOW}. Medium-wide view.

He offered burnt offerings on the altar: {ALTAR}, with a tall bright fire burning on top of it and a thick column of pale smoke rising straight up; before it {NOAH}, kneels with both arms raised, seen from behind and to one side. Nothing can be made out in the flames but burning wood. No animals in the picture. {ONE}. {NOBOW}. Medium-wide low-angle view.

Burnt offerings on the altar: four married couples kneeling together in a half circle on the mountainside around {ALTAR}, on which a fire burns and smoke rises, each husband with his wife beside him: {NOAH}, with {NOAH_WIFE}; {SHEM}, with {WIFE_S}; {HAM}, with {WIFE_H}; and {JAPHETH}, with {WIFE_J}. {EIGHT}. No animals in the picture. {NOBOW}. Wide view.

When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma: a column of pale smoke rising straight up from a small fire on a stone altar far below on a mountainside, climbing into a high clear sky where it meets {GLORY}. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOBOW}. Very wide low-angle view.

{EMPTY}. He said in His heart: {GLORY}, spreading wide and gentle over range upon range of mountains and green valleys, and tiny far below on a rocky mountain shoulder one thin thread of pale altar smoke rising straight up. No ark, no ship and no building in the picture. {NOPEOPLE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. {NOBOW}. Very wide high view.

Never again will I curse the ground because of man: a close view of two weathered hands of a man lifting a double handful of dark, rich, crumbling soil with small green shoots growing in it, golden light falling on the soil. Only the two hands and forearms of one man, no face. Close view.

Even though every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth: {NOAH}, kneeling alone on the ground with his head bowed low and his face hidden in both hands, golden light falling from above and his long dark shadow lying on the earth behind him. {ONE}. {NOLIGHTFIG}. Medium view.

And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done: a broad green valley in gentle golden light, full of life, with deer and wild cattle grazing beside a calm river, storks wading and flocks of birds wheeling above. {CALM}. {NOPEOPLE}. No boats. {NOBOW}. Very wide view.

{EMPTY}. As long as the earth endures: range beyond range of mountains, valleys, rivers and far plains stretching to a wide horizon under an immense clear sky at sunrise. {NOPEOPLE}. No buildings. {NOBOW}. Very wide high view from the air.

Seedtime: a farmer in a knee-length tunic of rough undyed wool, seen from behind, walking away from us down the dark furrows of a ploughed field at morning and scattering seed with a wide sweep of his arm from a cloth bag slung at his side. {ONE}. No buildings. {NOBOW}. Medium-wide view.

And harvest: a field of ripe golden barley in late sun, and in the foreground a woman in a long dress of rough undyed wool and a headcloth, bending to bind a thick sheaf of cut barley with a twist of straw, more sheaves standing behind her. {ONE}. No buildings. {NOBOW}. Medium view.

Cold: snow falling softly on a silent mountain valley, pine boughs heavy with snow, a frozen stream, and two deer standing in the snow with their breath steaming. Exactly two deer. {NOPEOPLE}. No buildings. Wide view.

And heat: a sun-scorched plain shimmering under a white noon sun, dry golden grass, and a single spreading tree in whose dark shade two oxen lie resting. Exactly two oxen. {NOPEOPLE}. No buildings. {NOBOW}. Wide view.

{EMPTY}. Summer: a very close view, filling the whole picture, of a vine heavy with clusters of ripe dark grapes among broad green leaves in bright warm sunlight, bees hovering at the fruit; behind the leaves only blurred green and sky. {NOPEOPLE}. Very close view.

card_notes: Every spoken word is Scripture: Genesis 8:1–22, complete.
notes: Text: Genesis 8:1-22 in full, no verses skipped or abridged. Speakers: N narrator, G the voice of God (8:16-17 and 8:21-22; the words of 8:21-22 are what the LORD 'said in His heart' and are voiced like His other speech). Noah does not speak in this chapter. Every used verse was read for typos in the snapshot: none found.
Still tags: T = from the text, I = inferred, D = dramatized. Still 'verses' are chapter:verse.

Faces and designs reused word for word from s01e02b and s01e02c: NOAH, NOAH_WIFE, SHEM, HAM, JAPHETH and their sheets, blocks GLORY, ARK, ARKFLOAT, INSIDE, WIFE_S, WIFE_H, WIFE_J, NOLAND, NODEAD, CALM. Noah stays the weathered man of about fifty (8:13 gives his 601st year; I, as decided in s01e02b). New blocks for Genesis 9 to reuse word for word: ARKREST (the ARK text with the bottom 'resting level on a broad shoulder of bare rock high among mountains'), ALTAR, DOORWAY, EIGHT, SONS8, NOBOW.
No rainbow appears anywhere in this unit (block NOBOW on every open sky): the bow is first given in Genesis 9:13. Any take with a rainbow is rejected at review.

Order of the waters, kept as the text gives it: the ark comes to rest in the seventh month (8:4) but the mountaintops are not seen until the tenth (8:5). So under 8:4 the ark settles on rock that is still under water (D1 underwater, D3 from above with the ridge showing through the water) and no land is seen above the surface until E2. The ground around the ark is wet until 8:13 and green only from 8:11 onward.
'The mountains of Ararat' (8:4) is a region, plural: no particular peak is identified and no snow-cone landmark is painted (I).

The window (8:6) and the covering (8:13): Genesis 6:16 and the ARK block leave the ark's sides windowless, so the window 'he had made' is painted as a small square shuttered hatch in the roof (block HATCH), and 'the covering' as roof planks that Noah lifts away (M3-M5). Both are I; the text gives neither position nor size.

The raven (8:7): the text says it kept flying back and forth and does not say it came back inside; it is shown flying over the water and wheeling above the ark, never re-entering. The dove is one white dove, called 'her' by the text. In 8:9 the dove finds only water, 'because the waters were still covering the surface of all the earth', although 8:5 has the mountaintops in view: the dove pictures show only water close around her and I4 shows flat water with a few far points of rock; the two verses are not harmonised further.
The olive leaf (8:11) is one leaf, not a branch or sprig: K2 and K3 must be checked at review. K5 (an olive tree on a hillside above the water) is I.

Leaving the ark (8:16-19): the text does not say who opened the door or how they came down; Noah pushes the door open (O2, I) and the sill lies level with a slope of rock (block DOORWAY, D), the building ramp having washed away in s01e02c. 'Kind by kind' (8:19): each kind walks or flies with its own kind. Whether the animals had young in the ark is not shown; P5 (a ewe with newborn lambs) pictures the command 'be fruitful and multiply' and is I.

The altar and offering (8:20): unhewn stones (I, after Exodus 20:25). The clean animals and birds stand beside the altar (S2: a ram, a young bull, a goat, two doves, following Leviticus as in s01e02c); no slaughter, knife or blood is shown and nothing but burning wood can be made out in the fire (S3). The family kneeling (S4) is D.

God is light only (GLORY), never a figure. 'The LORD smelled the pleasing aroma' is shown as smoke rising into the light (T1). 'Every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth' (T4) is shown as Noah bowed with his face hidden and his shadow behind him (D): no particular sin is pictured.
8:22: the farmer (U2) and the reaper (U3) are unnamed later people, seen from behind or bent over their work (I). Each of the eight named things has its own picture; the film ends on night.
